roomDerivation.name: all-zero-secret
roomDerivation.note: Edge case: a room secret of all-zero bytes derives normally - HKDF has no weak inputs.

roomDerivation.name: all-0xff-secret
roomDerivation.note: Edge case: a room secret of all-0xff bytes derives normally.

roomDerivation.name: typical-secret-1
roomDerivation.note: A representative room secret, reused across the credential/roster/signal groups below so those vectors trace back to one room.

roomDerivation.name: typical-secret-2
roomDerivation.note: A second representative secret, used as "a different room" in wrong-room negative cases elsewhere.

joinUrl.name: basic-no-policy
joinUrl.note: The common case: a secret and two relay hints, no access policy.

joinUrl.name: kith-policy-with-admitted-issuer
joinUrl.note: A kith-gated policy round-trips its admitted-issuer allow-list.

joinUrl.name: open-policy-has-no-admitted-list
joinUrl.note: An 'open' policy carries no admitted list at all - decodeJoinUrl must not invent one.

joinUrl.name: empty-relay-list
joinUrl.note: Edge case: an empty relay list is a valid, if useless, join URL.

joinUrl.name: decode-malformed-fragment
joinUrl.note: A fragment that is not valid base64url must be refused, not silently treated as an open room.

output.error: join URL fragment is not valid

joinUrl.name: decode-fragment-not-json
joinUrl.note: A fragment made entirely of valid base64url characters that decodes to bytes which are not valid JSON at all - the alphabet check alone is not enough; the decoded payload must actually parse.

output.error: join URL fragment is not valid

joinUrl.name: decode-payload-wrong-shape
joinUrl.note: A fragment that decodes to valid JSON of the wrong shape - no 's' secret field at all - must be refused, not treated as a room with an empty or undefined secret.

output.error: join URL carries a malformed secret

joinUrl.name: decode-secret-wrong-length
joinUrl.note: A fragment that decodes to valid JSON but carries a 16-byte secret (not 32) must be refused.

output.error: join URL carries a malformed secret

joinUrl.name: decode-policy-unknown-tier
joinUrl.note: A policy naming a tier outside open/ken/kith/kin must be refused, not silently dropped into an open room.

output.error: join URL carries an access policy at an unknown tier

deviceCredential.name: valid
deviceCredential.note: A credential signed by the participant, authorising one device, in one room, until an expiry.

deviceCredential.name: wrong-room
deviceCredential.note: The same, valid credential, checked against a different room id than the one it names.

deviceCredential.name: expired
deviceCredential.note: A credential whose expiry has already passed at verification time.

deviceCredential.name: tampered-signature
deviceCredential.note: The valid credential's device tag swapped for a different pubkey after signing - the signature no longer covers the tags it is checked against.

rosterEvent.name: valid
rosterEvent.note: A roster entry (with its device credential nested inside) encrypted to the room key and signed by the device.

rosterEvent.name: wrong-room-key
rosterEvent.note: The same event, decrypted with room 2's key instead of the room it was actually published to - NIP-44 decryption fails its MAC check and the decoder must return null, not throw.

rosterEvent.name: wrong-signing-device
rosterEvent.note: The entry names DEVICE_A as the authorised device, but a different device (holding no credential for this room) signed the event.

rosterEvent.name: tampered-outer-signature
rosterEvent.note: The valid roster event above with its own signature corrupted - id, pubkey, tags and content untouched. Decryption, the room match, and the entry.device === event.pubkey check would all still pass; only verifying the event's own signature catches this.

rosterEvent.name: forged-credential-signature
rosterEvent.note: The outer event is genuinely signed by DEVICE_IMPOSTOR, and entry.device matches it, but the nested credential (claiming PARTICIPANT_A authorised DEVICE_IMPOSTOR) is the valid DEVICE_A credential with its device tag swapped after signing - PARTICIPANT_A never signed this. Room, decrypt, the outer signature, and entry.device === event.pubkey all pass; only verifying the nested credential's own signature catches this.

signalWrap.name: offer
signalWrap.note: An SDP offer, gift-wrapped so the relay sees neither the SDP nor the sender's identity - only that someone sent something to the recipient.

signalWrap.name: ice-candidate
signalWrap.note: A trickled ICE candidate, wrapped the same way as an offer or answer.

signalWrap.name: wrong-recipient
signalWrap.note: The offer wrap above, opened by someone other than the intended recipient - the ECDH shared point differs, so the outer NIP-44 payload fails to authenticate and unwrapSignal must return null.

signalWrap.name: wrong-room
signalWrap.note: The offer wrap above, unwrapped correctly by the real recipient but checked against a room id the inner body does not name.

signalWrap.name: tampered-inner-signature
signalWrap.note: The offer's inner event with its own signature corrupted - id, pubkey, tags and content untouched - re-wrapped under a fresh (but otherwise ordinary) ephemeral key. The outer wrap decrypts fine, and inner.kind, body.roomId, and the addressed 'p' tag all still check out; only verifying the inner event's own signature catches this.

kindredProof.name: ken
kindredProof.note: A ken proof: the issuer vouches for GUEST at the 'ken' tier, in ROOM_1, until KINDRED_EXPIRES_AT. The room and the nonce are both inside the signed message - see canonicalMessage in src/access.ts - so a proof cannot be edited into another room, and two proofs on identical terms are still distinguishable. Pins the signed message layout, not any admission decision - see the accessEvaluation group for that.

kindredProof.name: kith
kindredProof.note: A kith proof: the issuer vouches for GUEST at the 'kith' tier, in ROOM_1, until KINDRED_EXPIRES_AT. The room and the nonce are both inside the signed message - see canonicalMessage in src/access.ts - so a proof cannot be edited into another room, and two proofs on identical terms are still distinguishable. Pins the signed message layout, not any admission decision - see the accessEvaluation group for that.

kindredProof.name: kin
kindredProof.note: A kin proof: the issuer vouches for GUEST at the 'kin' tier, in ROOM_1, until KINDRED_EXPIRES_AT. The room and the nonce are both inside the signed message - see canonicalMessage in src/access.ts - so a proof cannot be edited into another room, and two proofs on identical terms are still distinguishable. Pins the signed message layout, not any admission decision - see the accessEvaluation group for that.

accessEvaluation.name: open-room-admits-anyone
accessEvaluation.note: An open room admits any participant without a proof at all.

accessEvaluation.name: kith-room-admits-kith-proof
accessEvaluation.note: A kith-gated room admits a matching kith proof from a trusted issuer.

accessEvaluation.name: kith-room-admits-kin-proof
accessEvaluation.note: A kith-gated room also admits a kin proof - kin is closer than kith.

accessEvaluation.name: kith-room-rejects-ken-proof
accessEvaluation.note: A kith-gated room refuses a ken proof - ken is one-way recognition and never satisfies a kith gate ('tier too low').

accessEvaluation.name: kith-room-rejects-untrusted-issuer
accessEvaluation.note: A kith-gated room refuses a well-formed, correctly-signed kith proof from an issuer not on its allow-list.

accessEvaluation.name: kith-room-admits-issuer-via-upper-case-allow-list-entry
accessEvaluation.note: The allow-list names the trusted issuer (HOST) in upper-case hex; the proof itself is issued and signed normally, so its issuer field is the ordinary lower-case pubkey. Still admitted - an implementation that compares the allow-list entry to the issuer with an exact string match wrongly refuses this.

accessEvaluation.name: kith-room-admits-upper-case-issuer-against-lower-case-allow-list
accessEvaluation.note: The mirror image: the proof carries its own issuer field in upper-case hex - issuer is not part of the signed message (see canonicalMessage in src/access.ts), so upper-casing it does not disturb the signature - while the room's allow-list names HOST in the ordinary lower case. Still admitted.

accessEvaluation.name: kith-room-rejects-proof-for-another-room
accessEvaluation.note: A kith proof from the trusted issuer, at a sufficient tier, unexpired, naming the right participant - and minted for a different room. An implementation that does not compare proof.room to the room being joined admits a proof its issuer never granted here ('proof names another room').

accessEvaluation.name: kith-room-rejects-room-edited-into-the-proof
accessEvaluation.note: The same other-room proof with its `room` field rewritten to name this room. The room is inside the signed message, so rewriting it invalidates the signature ('bad signature') - an implementation that binds the room but leaves it out of canonicalMessage admits this.

accessEvaluation.name: kith-room-admits-proof-against-upper-case-room-id
accessEvaluation.note: The room id handed to evaluateAccess is upper-case hex naming the very room the proof was minted for. Hex identifiers are compared case-insensitively throughout - see the section of this README on that - so this is still admitted.

accessEvaluation.name: kith-room-rejects-tampered-signature
accessEvaluation.note: A kith proof from the trusted issuer, at a sufficient tier, unexpired, naming the right participant - identical to 'kith-room-admits-kith-proof' except its signature is garbage. Every check before the final schnorr verification passes; skip that check, or skip it entirely, and this is indistinguishable from a genuine proof.

turnCredential.name: coturn-known-vector
turnCredential.note: Cross-checked independently with Node's own crypto module (see src/turn.test.ts) - HMAC-SHA1('my-shared-secret', '1735776000:kithmoot') base64-encoded.

turnCredential.name: custom-device-name
turnCredential.note: A per-viewer name in place of the default.

turnCredential.name: fractional-seconds-floor
turnCredential.note: ttl and now are floored before being summed, so expiry is always a whole Unix second.

turnCredential.name: zero-ttl
turnCredential.note: Edge case: a zero-length TTL still mints a credential that expires immediately.
